result.title: The next cure for a fatal disease could already be sitting on a shelf #TEDTalks
A better future is actually possible — and we’re imagining it with the kids who’ll inherit it
The Surprising Beauty of Mosquitos | Felix Hol | TED
result.description:
Most people hate mosquitoes, but biotechnologist and TED Fellow Felix Hol thinks they're beautiful. He takes us inside his lab, where his team developed some unusual ways to study how these blood-sucking insects find us and feed so fast. He also explains why insecticides may send certain mosquitoes into overdrive — and how we can find smarter ways to curb the diseases they spread. (Recorded at TED Fellows Films on April 15, 2026)

result.title: The most teachable moments might happen when parents aren’t there #TEDTalks
result.description: Whether it’s micromanaging playtime, constantly hovering or incessantly texting, the adult takeover of childhood has created a crisis of anxiety in both children and parents, says Lenore Skenazy, cofounder and president of Let Grow, an organization dedicated to normalizing childhood independence. With wit and humor, she lays out the unexpected benefits of letting our kids be a bit more “free range” — and shows why the most teachable moments happen when parents aren’t there.

result.title: How to Make Friends (and Keep Them) | Sheridan Voysey | TED
result.description:
Who could you call at 2am when everything’s gone wrong? Friendship expert Sheridan Voysey believes we’re in a friendship recession, with many of us forgetting how to foster meaningful relationships. He explores three hidden barriers keeping us apart, why it feels harder to make friends as an adult — and how to nurture the deep connections that sustain us. (Recorded at TEDxSt Albans on October 15, 2025)
